# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Press the key that wears ᖉ first: any other touch
on the bomb while it waits is the fuse. Then the light below
names the cut.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | blue |
| green | red |
| yellow | yellow |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I need to convey the essential sequence to Deaf visually: press the specially marked key first, then use the lower light to determine the wire. The color mapping is blue→blue, green→red, yellow→yellow. Since Deaf cannot hear, I will use distinct gestures as visual instructions and rely on Deaf to relay the observed details to Blind.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "✊", "👇", "👍", "✌", "👌"])
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Press the key that wears ᖉ first: any other touch
on the bomb while it waits is the fuse. Then the light below
names the cut.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | blue |
| green | red |
| yellow | yellow |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Read the manual's complete instructions for this bomb, including what the display, light, keypad, and wires mean. Also establish with Deaf how Deaf will report colours, markings, and symbols to you, then relay the relevant bomb information to me.
Deaf says to Mute: I see display zero, green light, wires in order red yellow blue, and four keypad keys. Key 1 has an unfamiliar printed angular symbol, key 2 has a different unfamiliar printed symbol, key 3 has a third unfamiliar printed symbol, and key 4 has a fourth unfamiliar printed symbol. No digit entered. Your gestures were pointing up, fist, pointing down, thumbs up, victory, and OK.

The manual requires the marked key to be pressed before any other bomb contact. Deaf reports a green light, so the required wire color is red; with wires ordered red, yellow, blue, Blind must cut the first wire. I will use a clear gesture sequence for Deaf to relay: key 1, then press; green light; cut the red wire, which is wire 1. Deaf can describe these gestures to Blind aloud.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "✊", "✌", "🤜", "☝"])
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Press the key that wears ᖉ first: any other touch
on the bomb while it waits is the fuse. Then the light below
names the cut.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | blue |
| green | red |
| yellow | yellow |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Observed state: display 0, green light, wires position 1 red, position 2 yellow, position 3 blue. Four keys have distinct printed symbols that I cannot identify by touch. Please give the manual's exact rule and final action, including any required key position and wire position.

The observed green light maps to the red wire, which is position 1. The marked key must be pressed first; based on the established report, this is key position 1. I will reinforce the required order to Deaf so it can tell Blind: press key 1, then cut wire 1.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "🤜", "☝"])
```

TURN 4
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Press the key that wears ᖉ first: any other touch
on the bomb while it waits is the fuse. Then the light below
names the cut.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | blue |
| green | red |
| yellow | yellow |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Please use gestures to give the exact required action. Protocol: fist then position means press a key; open hand then position means cut a wire. Position markers are pointing up for 1, victory for 2, three-finger sign for 3, and open hand for 4. Deaf should relay every gesture by name and repeat the complete action.
Deaf says to Mute: Blind signalled one gesture: pointing up.

The required action is to press key position 1 first, then cut wire position 1. I will send Deaf the protocol sequence: fist, pointing up; open hand, pointing up. Using distinct symbols avoids confusing the action marker with the position marker.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤜", "☝", "✋", "☝"])
```

TURN 5
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Press the key that wears ᖉ first: any other touch
on the bomb while it waits is the fuse. Then the light below
names the cut.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | blue |
| green | red |
| yellow | yellow |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
System: the keypad opens
Deaf says to Mute: The keypad opened after digit 5 was entered.

The green light still requires cutting the red wire at position 1. The keypad-opening report does not establish which of the four keys bears ᖉ, and the manual makes that key’s position essential; I must not guess it. I will tell Deaf to visually locate ᖉ, report its position to Blind, and relay the already certain wire instruction using the established protocol.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✋", "☝"])
```
